result.summary: Adds a `-v2onlyclearnet` configuration option that disallows unencrypted v1 P2P connections on IPv4 and IPv6 networks. It skips outbound v1 connection attempts to clearnet peers, suppresses v1 downgrade reconnections after failed v2 handshakes, and disconnects inbound clearnet peers that connect with v1 transport. Encrypted overlay networks (Tor, I2P, CJDNS) and non-routable local addresses remain permitted to use v1.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core automatically initiates or falls back to unencrypted v1 transport for clearnet peers and accepts inbound v1 connections by default. Users wishing to protect message contents from passive on-path observers such as ISPs cannot enforce transport encryption across IPv4 and IPv6 without disabling clearnet entirely.
evidence: PR description: 'Currently 70% of reachable nodes in network supporting v2 (according to https://21.ninja/reachable-nodes/node-service-share/ and https://bitnodes.io/nodes). Also found 81% of addresses supporting v2 in the addrman of nodes I checked'
result.scope_notes: Touches net connection selection and inbound message processing in net_processing to drop v1 clearnet peers.
result.changed_since_previous: Instead of requiring `-listen=0` to prevent unencrypted inbound traffic, listening is now supported and inbound v1 clearnet connections are disconnected during message processing. Destinations delegated to name proxies are also addressed by assuming worst-case clearnet and requiring v2.
result.card: Adds the `-v2onlyclearnet` configuration flag to forbid unencrypted v1 P2P traffic over IPv4 and IPv6. Today, nodes fall back to or accept unencrypted v1 clearnet connections, exposing message contents to passive observers such as ISPs unless clearnet is turned off entirely. The option disables outbound v1 clearnet attempts, suppresses v1 fallback on handshake failure, and disconnects inbound v1 clearnet peers during the version handshake, while leaving Tor, I2P, CJDNS, and local connections unaffected. Network measurements cited by the author show roughly 70% of reachable nodes and over 80% of sampled addrman addresses support BIP324 v2 transport.

risk.why: Faulty peer transport filtering could cause unexpected peer disconnections or isolate nodes that enable the option.
